question.worked_solution:
From the identity $1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta ,$ with $\theta =2x+\frac{\pi }{5},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}1+{tan}^{2}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{5})={sec}^{2}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{5}).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{{tan}^{2}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{5})\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{5})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{5})}\,\text{d}x & = \\ \int \frac{1}{[{tan}^{2}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{5})+1]\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{5})}\,\text{d}x & = \\ \int \frac{1}{{sec}^{2}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{5})\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{5})}\,\text{d}x & = \\ \int \frac{{cos}^{2}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{5})}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{5})}\,\text{d}x & = \\ \int \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{5})\text{d}x & = \\ \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{5})+C & .\end{aligned}
$$
